lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: counting pretend money

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 3 — spending and comparing
objective: Learners find the value of groups of like pretend coins by repeated addition, combine the groups into one total, and compare the total against a pretend price.
scenario: Dev is a made-up third grader counting a handful of play coins for a pretend market game: 3 quarters, 4 dimes, and 2 nickels. A quarter is $0.25, a dime is $0.10, and a nickel is $0.05. The coins are toy coins from a classroom set.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Start with Dev's three play quarters at $0.25 each.

prompts.text: What are Dev's three quarters worth altogether?

tasks.directions: Now count Dev's dimes as their own group before mixing anything together, then bring all three groups into a single total.

prompts.text: What are Dev's four dimes worth altogether?
What is the value of all of Dev's coins together?

tasks.directions: Dev finds 5 more play pennies, worth $0.01 each, and wants a pretend market item priced at $1.50.

prompts.text: What is the value of all of Dev's coins now?
Is that enough for the $1.50 pretend item?

tasks.directions: Dev counted coins in groups rather than one at a time.

prompts.text: Why is counting the quarters as a group easier than counting every coin one by one?

remediation: When a learner counts every coin as one unit, sort the play coins into three piles by type and count each pile in its own skip-count aloud, so quarters are counted by twenty-fives rather than by ones.
extension: Ask the learner which single extra play coin would take Dev from $1.30 to exactly $1.50, and to show why no other single coin works.
